1 حَبَقَ , (S, Msb, K,) said of a goat, (Lth, TA,) or mostly said of the camel and of the goat, (K,) and sometimes of a man, (TA,) or حَبَقَتْ, said of a she-goat, (Msb,) aor.
حَبِقَ , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. حَبِقٌ (S, K) and حَبْقٌ (Msb, K) and حُبَاقٌ, (K,) He, or she, broke wind. (S, Msb, K.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] يَحْبِقُونَ عَلَى فُلَانٍ (tropical:) They revile such a one; and act in an ignorant, or a silly, or foolish, and a wrong manner towards him. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
